speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient with a limp and localized pain, but no fever. To help you, can you tell me exactly where on your body the pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain is in the left knee but he is favoring that leg, can you point to exactly where it hurts most when you touch it? Is the pain sharp or dull, and does it wake you up at night? Also, have you noticed any swelling, warmth, or redness in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).

The previous suggestion of a migraine is incorrect given the specific mechanical limp and localized knee pain; in children, hip pathology often refers pain to the knee. I need to confirm if pain extends to the groin or thigh and check for limited internal hip rotation.
